name: Ho Nguyen Trung
role: Eldest son of Hồ Quý Ly; general, military engineer, architect and writer - one of Đại Việt's rare all-round technical geniuses
known_facts: Before the war he warned: 'Thần không ngại đánh, chỉ sợ lòng dân có theo hay không theo mà thôi' - fearing the people would not follow the Hồ
Invented and directed the making of súng thần cơ (an improved firearm / hand-cannon) and thuyền cổ lâu (large two-tier war ships)
With these, Đại Việt's military technology outmatched the Ming on land and river - but a dynasty without the people's heart could not be saved by superior weapons
Chief engineer (tổng công trình sư) of Thành nhà Hồ and of the northern dyke/irrigation works during the Hồ reforms

Thành nhà Hồ: outer walls and four gates of dressed blue-green limestone, some blocks over 6 metres long and about 20 tonnes, dry-laid without mortar, standing 600+ years through earthquakes and bombing
About 20,000 cubic metres of stone and nearly 100,000 cubic metres of earth were moved; the citadel was built in only three months (early to spring 1397)
Archaeologists found round stone balls proving he used roller/pulley (windlass) techniques to move the huge blocks
Founder of the memoir genre in Vietnamese narrative prose
A man who prized practice, mathematics and natural science over the poetry-contest scholarship of his day - captured by the Ming, his genius was lost to Vietnam
Named beside eunuch-architect Nguyễn An (chief builder of Beijing's Forbidden City) as talents produced by the Hồ reforms and taken by the Ming
interpretation: Early-15th-century Hồ-era Đại Việt scholar-engineer/officer dress, based on the user reference.
unknowns: No verified contemporary life portrait survives
